facts.raw_span: slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for: synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

concepts.why: The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement, tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles, and positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies support the diagnosis of apocrine carcinoma.

aliases: Extramammary Paget Disease of the Axilla
concepts.why: The presence of a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla and positive immunohistochemistry for cytokeratin 20 and GCDFP15 support the diagnosis of extramammary Paget disease.

The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement, tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles, and positive immunohistochemistry for GATA3 and estrogen receptor support the diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma.

The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement, tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles, and positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin and cytokeratin 20 support the diagnosis of syringocystadenocarcinoma.
The presence of swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy and mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles support the diagnosis of an axillary cyst.
The presence of a slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla and a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla support the diagnosis of a lipoma.
The presence of swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy and mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles support the diagnosis of an axillary abscess.
The presence of progressive infiltration of the overlying skin and a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla support the diagnosis of cellulitis.
The presence of cytokeratin8/18-positive and MNF116-positive tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node suggests metastasis from a breast carcinoma.
